messages:
maria: heads-up, canary in us-west-2 is crashlooping after the last rollout. seeing OOMKilled on the encoder pods and HPA is ramping up/down in a loop. customers reporting higher latencies (~10-15%) on inference requests.

maria: deploy-bot shows rollout-id=rl-2026-03-15-09:15, canary=5%. I think the new encoder change introduced larger mem spikes under cold start. stack shows preStop + heavy finalizer maybe blocking shutdown.

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollout rl-2026-03-15-09:15 started for service/encoder-svc (canary 5%) :rocket:

incident-bot: paging oncall @maya-oncall for severity=high (inference errors, customer impact). See /runbook/deploy-failures for next steps.

maya-oncall: I got the page, jumping in. maria, can you paste `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=encoder -o wide` and `kubectl describe pod` for one of the failing pods?

maria: pasted outputs below:

```
$ kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=encoder -o wide
NAME                          READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE     NODE
encoder-svc-canary-7d9c2      0/1     CrashLoopBackOff  6    8m   ip-10-0-3-44
encoder-svc-canary-9f2b1      1/1     Running           0    7m   ip-10-0-3-45
```

```
$ kubectl describe pod encoder-svc-canary-7d9c2 -n prod
Events:
  Normal  Pulling    2m  kubelet Pulling image
  Normal  Created    2m  kubelet Created container
  Warning BackOff    1m  kubelet Back-off restarting failed container
  Warning OOMKilled  1m  kubelet Container killed due to OOM
...
```

maria: logs show encoder OOM during large batch deserialization on startup. also saw SIGTERM then container killed before graceful shutdown completed: terminationGracePeriodSeconds=5 in the manifest.

sahil: that grace period is tiny. if preStop does cleanup + flush + finalizer, 5s would definitely not be enough and could cause in-flight memory to spike or the process to die mid-cleanup. why did we land 5s?

jess: it was part of the manifest size-reduction PR (to speed up drains). we underestimated the shutdown sequence of the encoder.

maya-oncall: whether this is the cause or not, customers are impacted. mitigation options: 1) pause rollout/kill canary, 2) raise terminationGracePeriodSeconds and restart pods, 3) toggle feature flag to disable new encoder variant, 4) undo rollout (rollback). Thoughts?

maria: recommend short-term: abort the canary and flip the feature flag to route canary traffic back to the old encoder. then patch manifest to increase terminationGracePeriodSeconds to 60 and bump livenessProbe initialDelay/period. Finally, set HPA minReplicas to avoid oscillation during the fix.

devops: I can patch HPA and manifest. quick commands: 
```
# set HPA min to 2 to avoid scale-to-zero churn
kubectl patch hpa encoder-svc -n prod -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2}}'

# increase termination grace
kubectl patch deployment encoder-svc -n prod --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/terminationGracePeriodSeconds","value":60}]'

# undo rollout if we want to go back
kubectl rollout undo deployment/encoder-svc -n prod --to-revision=41
```

maria: doing the feature-flag flip now: @featureflagbot disable encoder-v2 on prod (canary). will report when done.

featureflagbot: FeatureFlag encoder-v2 disabled in prod. Targeting 100% rollback of canary traffic within ~30s.

maria: canary traffic now at baseline. error rate dropping from 8% to 1.2% on requests to encoder path.

maya-oncall: good. devops, please apply the HPA patch and terminate the problematic pod gracefully once the new grace period is in place. we want to avoid killing it with OOM rather than restart.

devops: patch applied: minReplicas=2. patch confirmed in HPA status. upgrading terminationGracePeriodSeconds to 60 on the deployment.

devops: I'm cordoning node ip-10-0-3-44 to avoid new pods landing while we drain it: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-3-44`

devops: now doing `kubectl drain ip-10-0-3-44 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` to trigger graceful reschedules.

maria: after drain, restarted the canary pods. the ones that come up now have higher memory headroom and the crashloop stopped.

jess: we should still roll back the deploy in case there are hidden regressions. I'd prefer a full rollback to the previous stable revision and then a controlled rollout after we increase shutdown grace and add a fast-fail health check for large batch memory usage.

maya-oncall: agree. let's rollback the deployment to revision 41. devops, can you perform the rollback and monitor errors/latency for the next 15 minutes? I'll coordinate customer comms.

devops: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/encoder-svc -n prod --to-revision=41` executed. rollout status shows 100% of pods ready under revision 41.

maria: metrics look good: p95 latency back to normal, error rate under 0.5%. HPA oscillation stopped because minReplicas prevented aggressive downscaling during instability.

incident-bot: incident severity downgraded to medium. Auto-attach runbook: /runbook/deploy-failures, postmortem suggested.

maya-oncall: I'll open a postmortem and assign owners: root-cause (maria/jess) and remediation (sahil/devops). action items: increase terminationGracePeriodSeconds default for encoders, add a livenessProbe safeguard to reject large-batch initialization within X seconds, add an eval to CI to simulate cold-start memory usage, and add an HPA policy guard to avoid oscillation during rollouts.

jess: also recommend adding a pre-flight check in the rollout job to ensure terminationGracePeriodSeconds >= 30 for workloads that use preStop finalizers.

maria: noted. I'll draft the postmortem and share the timeline. thanks everyone for quick responses.

maya-oncall: handing back to oncall rotation. closing this thread once postmortem link is added. :white_check_mark:
